name: tech_house_groove
label: Tech house (grammar engine, any song)
what: Tech house for any song, through the grammar engine so the variety bank can vary it (the "tech_house" pack is the first song's fixed engine, kept only for the Friends regression build). Four on the floor with a punchy kick light in the sub, clap with a snare layer on 2 and 4, an open hat on every off-beat, swung 16th hats, syncopated percussion and low ghost rims, a rolling 16th bass that leaves each kick's 16th free and moves to the octave, fifth or minor seventh, a sub only under the drops, short dry stabs. Short breaks, long DJ-friendly intro and outro.
levels_note: The person's approved Friends tech-house mix (v15, by ear): clap -3.5, hats -3.5, FX -2.5, arp -2.5 dB; the vocal up 1 dB as in their house balance (styles/house.json levels_note).

kick_sub_shelf.why: tech house keeps the kick light in the sub so the bassline carries the low end (Beatportal); the same shelf the person chose on house master B

sources: https://www.beatportal.com/articles/692607-step-by-step-guide-to-producing-tech-house-like-fisher-chris-lake-cloonee-and-michael-bibi (most tech house at 120 to 128 bpm; a punchy kick with minimal sub because the bassline carries the low end; off-beat hats and syncopated shakers; small fills every 8 or 16 bars; short breakdowns; the bass sidechained to the kick)

https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/beat-dissected/deep-tech-house/ (125 to 130 bpm, swing 60 to 65 %, clap and snare layered on 2 and 4, an open hat on every off-beat, shaker 16ths with velocity changes, a quiet ghost snare in unusual places)

https://theproducerschool.com/blogs/featured-blogs/5-tech-house-bass-patterns-every-producer-needs-to-master (rolling 8ths and 16ths with tight transients, syncopated off-beat notes, a move to the fourth or fifth in bar 3 of 4 resolving to the root)
https://loststoriesacademy.com/blogs-and-tutorials/what-makes-a-track-dj-friendly (16 or 32 bar mix-in intro: kick, hats or percussion, minimal bass)
opinion: swing 0.58 sits under Attack's 60 to 65 % for deep tech house so a straight-sung pop vocal does not fight the hats; the range 124 to 128 is where the three sources overlap
